extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing fiction writers (novelists, short-story writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, process-focused advice for fiction writers on habits, idea capture, revision, and experimenting with craft to sustain long-term productivity and overcome blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thinking Time Over Writing Time
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of time you spend writing isn't necessarily as important as the time spent thinking about what you are going to write.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize planning, reflection, and problem-solving about the work before and between writing sessions rather than equating productivity solely with hours spent typing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture Every Idea Immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep notebooks/pens everywhere; 'hasn't lost a single idea or scene fragment in twenty years.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record idea fragments the moment they occur (physical notebook or quick notes). Treat idea capture as a non-negotiable habit to build a long-term reservoir of material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train Your Subconscious
rubrics_metrics.description: Set intentions before sleep about story problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre-sleep mental framing or rituals to prime creative problem-solving; employ the subconscious to work on story issues between active sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write During Peak Energy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mornings for drafts, afternoons for revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify daily energy rhythms and schedule tasks accordingly: tackle original drafting during high-energy periods and save lower-energy or analytical tasks (revision) for later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Healthy Habits
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited drinking, early bedtimes, exercise, less social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate lifestyle routines that support sustained creative work—sleep, exercise, moderation of substances, and reduced time-wasters—because physical and mental health affect writing consistency and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Love Revision Unconditionally
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace revision as essential and positive; expect imperfect first drafts and commit to iterative improvement rather than seeking perfection on the first pass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let Each Novel Guide Its Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt approach based on each project's demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rigid, one-size-fits-all methods; tailor workflow, pacing, and techniques to the specific needs, scale, and temperament of each book or project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment with New Techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: When stuck: change environment, switch locations, change fonts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete experiments—physical location changes, different tools or visual presentation, and other small shocks—to break blocks and discover new possibilities for the work.
